text: Databases store and organise information so we can find it quickly. In a relational database, data is kept in tables with rows and columns, like a spreadsheet. We use SQL to write queries, which are requests for specific information. Good data modeling helps us plan the structure before we add data. Indexes make searches much faster. However, not all databases work this way. NoSQL databases are more flexible and store data differently, often without fixed tables. They are useful for large amounts of changing data. Choosing between SQL and NoSQL depends on your needs.
